geometry.fact: Occupancy/coverage first, then cell-centred signed distance to a circle (negative inside), abs(SDF)<=dx narrow-band proximity, and local SDF-gradient normals with perpendicular tangents. It was a fixed 6x6 Cartesian carrier, not CAD topology.
geometry.storage: Float arrays for coverage/SDF and orientation components/strength on every lattice cell; edge fields were derived on implicit four-neighbor adjacency.
geometry.downstream: Orientation-weighted one-step diffusion-like transfer and later local constitutive frames.

material.fact: A separate interior orientation/direction carrier, initially constant, then region-tagged, then two seeded directions propagated by deterministic four-neighbor averaging for eight fixed sweeps.
material.storage: Ox, Oy, Strength arrays plus a descriptive rule.
material.downstream: Geometry/material orientation composition, anisotropic edge weights, and tangent/normal constitutive response.

authority.fact: Local confidence/ownership for composing geometry-derived and material-derived carriers: geometry confidence came from SDF proximity (with a floor), material confidence from explicit strength or a heterogeneous left-high/right-low map. It was not load direction, source ownership, or a PDE boundary-condition field.
authority.storage: GeometryConfidence and MaterialConfidence scalar arrays, independently built in M20.
authority.downstream: Hard winner/tie blending, material usage scaling, optional transport feedback; later evidence supported narrow coupling-specific constitutive modulation, not whole-response scaling or iteration policy.

supported: SDF supplied proximity and deterministic orientation not identical to occupancy.
Explicit geometry orientation changed the same local downstream operator and improved circle-boundary tangential fidelity in that fixture.
Separate geometry and material carriers were computationally distinguishable; seeded fixed-pass material transport reduced a hand-created region seam.
Explicit heterogeneous confidence changed carrier coupling; coupling-specific authority perturbations preserved local constitutive semantics better than scalar whole-response attenuation.
Tiny fixed correction loops reduced the experiment's mismatch metric with diminishing returns.
speculative: The 6x6 circle one-step metrics did not demonstrate a PDE solver or preconditioner advantage.
Seed transport was a hand-designed fixed-sweep organizer, not a physical material law.
Confidence maps were synthetic policies, not inferred or validated boundary-condition authority.
Later global-consistency loops explicitly avoided matrix assembly and generic convergence, so they do not establish scalable continuum solve behavior.
obsolete: Coverage/SDF as the primary representation of exact boundary identity and normals is obsolete where Aetheris exact BRep+CIR supplies analytic topology/geometry.
Inferring cut occupancy or interface orientation by sampling is obsolete for cut cells where exact cut metadata exists.
Fixed 6x6 implicit topology and circle-specific tangent construction are fixture assumptions, not production Continuum requirements.
What remains useful is the separation of geometry, material, and confidence/policy carriers and the demand that coupling stay explicit.
